newsitem.title: SYRIA: EU envoy in talks with Syrians on peace initiative.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy in talks with Syrians on peace initiative.

text.p: The European Union's Middle East envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos opened talks in Damascus on Wednesday with Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara on a formula to revive Damascus's stalled peace talks with Israel.
EU officials said Moratinos would clarify some misunderstanding on a peace initiative proposed by the EU to Syria last month during a visit by Moratinos.
The EU formula, which aims at narrowing the gap in the positions of Israel and Arabs in the negotiations, calls for "full Israeli withdrawal from the occupied Arab lands in return for full security."

"There has been some misunderstanding about the formula with some saying that security would only be granted to Israel while the initiative calls for equal and mutual security for all," the EU official said.
"Mr. Moratinos will explain the formula to remove any misunderstanding," he said.
The United States is the main sponsor of the Arab-Israeli peace talks which opened in Madrid in 1991 but Syria and other Arab states support a greater European role in the negotiations.
Israel has held sporadic peace talks with Syria since 1991 but the negotiations were blocked over the fate of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East War.
No talks were held since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu came to power in June.
Syria has strongly condemned Netanyahu for refusing to swap the occupied Arab lands for peace -- a formula on which the Arab-Israeli peace negotiations were based.

Damascus also rejected Netanyahu's call for resuming the peace talks with Syria which broke off in March 1996 without preconditions and said negotiations should restart from the point at which they left off with Israel's previous government.
Syria said that Israel's labour-led government which was defeated by Netanyahu in elections in May 1996 had agreed to withdraw fully from the Golan.
